_how: Flavor Trivia (added 16 Nov 2026). One set per date (Nairobi time). Each set: theme, img (photo for the card), qs = 10 questions. Each question: q, a (4 options), c (index of the right option, 0-3), x (one line shown after answering), s (optional story slug for 'Read our story'). Every answer checked against 2+ sources before it goes in. Week: Mon Music, Tue Art & Film, Wed African Business, Thu Countries, Fri Awards, Sat Sport, Sun History. A day with no set simply hides the Trivia card.

qs.q: Bien, Savara, Chimano and Polycarp made up which Kenyan band?
qs.x: They started as an a cappella trio at Upper Hill School, and guitarist Polycarp joined later.

qs.q: Manu Dibango's 1972 hit "Soul Makossa" came from which country?
qs.x: It started life as a B-side, recorded for Cameroon's hosting of the 1972 Africa Cup of Nations.

qs.q: Which Afrobeat pioneer entered the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2026?
qs.x: He went in under the Early Influence award. Sade was inducted the same year.

qs.q: Wizkid's "Made in Lagos" came out in which year?
qs.x: It was due on 15 October 2020, but he pushed it to 30 October because of the End SARS protests.

qs.q: The rapper and producer tg.blk is from which Kenyan city?
qs.x: She taught herself to rap and produce in her bedroom, on GarageBand.

qs.q: Which South African singer was known as "Mama Africa"?
qs.x: Born in Johannesburg in 1932, she spent about 30 years in exile for speaking out against apartheid.

qs.q: Burna Boy won his first Grammy with which album?
qs.x: It won Best Global Music Album in 2021, a year after African Giant lost in the same category.

qs.q: Tyla won the first-ever Grammy for Best African Music Performance with which song?
qs.x: It was the category's first year, at the 2024 Grammys, and she beat Burna Boy and Davido to it.

qs.q: "Jerusalema" by Master KG featuring Nomcebo is sung in which language?
qs.x: Burna Boy later jumped on the song for its remix.

qs.q: Diamond Platnumz founded which record label?
qs.x: It's based in Dar es Salaam, and its artists have included Zuchu and Mbosso.

qs.q: Lupita Nyong'o won her Oscar for which film?
qs.x: It was her first feature film role. She won Best Supporting Actress in 2014.

qs.q: Who directed "Rafiki", the first Kenyan feature film at Cannes?
qs.x: Kenya's film board banned it at home just before its 2018 Cannes premiere.

qs.q: FESPACO, Africa's biggest and oldest film festival, is held in which city?
qs.x: It started in 1969 and runs every two years in Burkina Faso's capital.

qs.q: In Thandiwe Muriu's photo series "Camo", the women…
a: Blend into a background of the same fabric
qs.x: She's a self-taught Nairobi photographer who picked up a camera at 14.

qs.q: Who directed the Kenyan film "Supa Modo"?
qs.x: It premiered at the 2018 Berlin film festival and was Kenya's Oscar entry that year.

qs.q: Ghanaian sculptor El Anatsui makes his famous shimmering tapestries out of…
qs.x: He flattens liquor-bottle caps and stitches them together with copper wire.

qs.q: Ousmane Sembène, called the "father of African cinema", was from which country?
qs.x: He was a novelist first, and turned to film so more people could reach his stories.

qs.q: Which South African film won the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film in 2006?
qs.x: It was the first South African film ever to win an Oscar.

qs.q: What was Netflix's first African original series?
qs.x: The South African spy thriller, starring Pearl Thusi, premiered in February 2020.

qs.q: Nollywood is the film industry of which country?
qs.x: By number of films made, it's the second-biggest film industry in the world, after India's.

qs.q: Safaricom launched M-Pesa in which year?
qs.x: It went live on 6 March 2007. "Pesa" is Swahili for money.

qs.q: Tusker beer is named after…
a: The elephant that killed co-founder George Hurst
qs.x: Hurst died on an elephant hunt in 1923, and his brother Charles named the beer in his memory.

qs.q: Bata, the shoe brand many people assume is Kenyan, was founded in which present-day country?
qs.x: The Baťa siblings started it in Zlín in 1894.

qs.q: The very first Nando's opened in 1987 in which city?
qs.x: It started in Rosettenville, a Johannesburg suburb, and was named after co-founder Fernando Duarte's son.

qs.q: What does MTN stand for?
qs.x: The Johannesburg-based network started out in the 90s as M-Cell.

qs.q: Which airline calls itself "The Pride of Africa"?
qs.x: KQ started using the line after its public share offer in 1996.

qs.q: Amarula cream liqueur is made from the fruit of which tree?
qs.x: Elephants love marula fruit too, which is why there's one on the bottle.

qs.q: In 2019, which became the first African tech startup to list on the New York Stock Exchange?
qs.x: It began trading as JMIA on 12 April 2019, while staff in Lagos rang a bell at the same moment.

qs.q: Tecno, one of Africa's best-selling phone brands, is owned by a company from which country?
qs.x: Its parent, Transsion, is based in Shenzhen and also owns Infinix and itel.

qs.q: Africa's biggest cement producer belongs to which billionaire?
qs.x: Dangote Cement runs in 10 African countries. Rabiu's BUA is a big rival.

qs.q: Which African country has the most people?
qs.x: Over 230 million people at the last count, the biggest population on the continent by a long way.

qs.q: What is the official capital of Tanzania?
qs.x: Dar is still the biggest city and business hub, but parliament moved to Dodoma in 1996.

qs.q: Which is Africa's biggest country by land area?
qs.x: About 2.38 million km², most of it Sahara. DR Congo is a close second.

qs.q: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
qs.x: Lesotho is an enclave, a whole country sitting inside another one.

qs.q: Africa's newest country became independent in 2011. Which one?
qs.x: It split from Sudan on 9 July 2011 after a referendum where nearly 99% voted to leave.

qs.q: South Africa has how many capital cities?
qs.x: Pretoria runs the government, Cape Town has parliament, and Bloemfontein has the courts.

qs.q: Which country grows the most cocoa in the world?
qs.x: It has led world production since the late 1970s, well ahead of neighbouring Ghana.

qs.q: Which country's flag has an AK-47 on it?
qs.x: It's the only national flag in the world with a modern rifle, crossed with a hoe on an open book.

qs.q: Which country is known as the "Land of a Thousand Hills"?
qs.x: In French it's "Pays des Mille Collines".

qs.q: Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain, is in which country?
qs.x: It sits right by the Kenyan border, but the whole mountain is in Tanzania. It stands 5,895 m tall.

qs.q: Burna Boy won his first Grammy for which album?
qs.x: It won Best Global Music Album in 2021, a year after African Giant lost to Angélique Kidjo.

qs.q: Wizkid got his first Grammy for his part on which song?
qs.x: Beyoncé's "Brown Skin Girl" won Best Music Video in 2021, the same night Burna won his first.

qs.q: Tems won her first Grammy for which song?
qs.x: The Future and Drake song samples her track "Higher". It won Best Melodic Rap Performance in 2023.

qs.q: Who won the very first Grammy for Best African Music Performance, in 2024?
qs.x: "Water" beat Burna Boy, Davido, Asake, Olamide and Ayra Starr in the category's first year.

qs.q: South Africa's Black Coffee won a Grammy in 2022 in which category?
qs.x: He won for "Subconsciously", his first nomination and first win.

qs.q: Who is the only African player ever to win the Ballon d'Or?
qs.x: He won it in 1995, the first year non-Europeans could be voted for. He later became Liberia's president.

qs.q: Who was the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize?
qs.x: The Kenyan environmentalist won it in 2004 for her work on sustainable development, democracy and peace.

qs.q: Who was the first Black African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
qs.x: The Nigerian playwright won it in 1986.

qs.q: Abdulrazak Gurnah, the 2021 Nobel Literature winner, was born on which island?
qs.x: He left Zanzibar at 18 after the 1964 revolution and became a writer and professor in England.

qs.q: Five-time Grammy winner Angélique Kidjo is from which country?
qs.x: She was born in 1960, when the country was still called Dahomey.

qs.q: Eliud Kipchoge ran the first marathon under two hours in which city?
qs.x: He ran 1:59:40 on 12 October 2019. It doesn't count as a world record because of the special pacing.

qs.q: Abebe Bikila won the 1960 Olympic marathon in Rome running…
qs.x: He was the first Black African to win Olympic gold, and he won again in Tokyo four years later.

qs.q: Which was the first African team to reach a men's World Cup semi-final?
qs.x: They beat Portugal 1-0 in the 2022 quarter-final in Qatar.

qs.q: Which country has won the most Africa Cup of Nations titles?
qs.x: Seven titles, the last in 2010. Cameroon are next with five.

qs.q: David Rudisha set his 1:40.91 800m world record at which Olympics?
qs.x: He led from start to finish and became the first man to run 800m under 1:41.

qs.q: Kenya's men's rugby sevens team is nicknamed…
qs.x: Shujaa is Swahili for courage or heroism.

qs.q: Faith Kipyegon has won three Olympic golds in which event?
qs.x: Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, the first athlete to win three Olympic 1500m titles.

qs.q: Which three countries will co-host AFCON 2027?
qs.x: The Pamoja bid won in September 2023. It's the first time any of the three will host.

qs.q: What is the nickname of Kenya's national football team?
qs.x: It comes from harambee, the Kenyan tradition of pulling together for a common cause.

qs.q: Before the 2022 semi-final, which African teams had reached a World Cup quarter-final?
qs.x: Cameroon in 1990, Senegal in 2002 and Ghana in 2010 all went out at that stage.

qs.q: On what date did Kenya become independent?
qs.x: June 1963 was self-rule (Madaraka). Kenya became a republic exactly a year after independence, in 1964.

qs.q: In 1957, which became the first sub-Saharan African country to win independence?
qs.x: Kwame Nkrumah led the Gold Coast to independence on 6 March 1957 and renamed it Ghana.

qs.q: Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 prison years on which island?
qs.x: The island sits off Cape Town. He walked free in 1990.

qs.q: At the Battle of Adwa in 1896, Ethiopia defeated which European army?
qs.x: Emperor Menelik II's victory on 1 March 1896 kept Ethiopia independent.

qs.q: The Organisation of African Unity was founded in 1963 in which city?
qs.x: 32 countries signed its charter on 25 May 1963, which is why 25 May is Africa Day.

qs.q: Mansa Musa, famous for his gold-filled trip to Mecca in 1324, ruled which empire?
qs.x: He handed out so much gold passing through Cairo that people talked about it for generations.

qs.q: Zimbabwe takes its name from…
qs.x: Great Zimbabwe, the stone city near Masvingo. The name is usually traced to the Shona for "houses of stone".

qs.q: Which Kenyan town is called the oldest and best-preserved Swahili settlement in East Africa?
qs.x: Lamu Old Town has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001.

qs.q: The railway from Mombasa to Lake Victoria got which nickname?
qs.x: Critics in Britain called it a lunatic line because of its cost and the lives lost building it.

qs.q: Which Mau Mau leader has a statue on Kimathi Street in Nairobi?
qs.x: He was hanged at Kamiti Prison on 18 February 1957. The statue went up 50 years later, in 2007.

qs.q: Bien's new album "Alusa Continua" plays on his middle name and which old rallying cry?
qs.x: Alusa is his middle name. A luta continua means the struggle continues.

qs.q: Bien is the first African artist signed to which Atlanta label?
qs.x: It's the label behind Migos and Lil Baby, and Alusa Continua is his first album with them.

qs.q: In Gikuyu, what does the word "mugithi" mean?
qs.x: It's named after the dance, where the whole room holds the hips of the person in front and snakes around.

qs.q: Benga music is most closely tied to which Kenyan community?
qs.x: Its bouncy guitar lines took off in the 1960s and 70s, with D.O. Misiani among its big names.

qs.q: Which Kenyan duo's "Unbwogable" became the anthem of the 2002 election?
qs.x: The title mixes English with the Dholuo word bwogo, to scare, so it means unshakeable. The NARC campaign made it its song.

qs.q: Rema's "Calm Down" got a remix with which American singer?
qs.x: The remix took it past a billion Spotify streams, a first for a song by an African lead artist.

qs.q: Amapiano was born in which country?
qs.x: The name means "the pianos" in isiZulu, after its signature keys. The log drum is its other trademark.

qs.q: Bongo Flava is the pop sound of which country?
qs.x: It mixes hip hop and R&B with taarab and dansi, and it's mostly sung in Swahili.

qs.q: The guitar legend Ali Farka Touré was from which country?
qs.x: He's often called the African John Lee Hooker, and he won three Grammys, the last one after he died.

qs.q: Sofiya Nzau's global hit "Mwaki", made with Brazilian producer Zerb, is sung in which language?
qs.x: Mwaki means fire. Sofiya is from Murang'a, and her husband pushed her to sing it in her mother tongue.

qs.q: Which Kenyan film won Best Film at the 2026 Africa Movie Academy Awards?
qs.x: Vincho Nchogu's debut also won Best Film in an African Language and Best Debut Feature.

qs.q: Floyd Norman, who got an honorary Oscar this month, was the first Black animator at which studio?
qs.x: Disney hired him in 1956, at 21. His first job was on Sleeping Beauty.

qs.q: Neema Ngelime, whose documentary won five awards at Durban FilmMart before it's even shot, is from which country?
qs.x: She's a documentary photographer too, and the main shoot is planned for 2027.

qs.q: Lupita Nyong'o's 2009 documentary "In My Genes" is about…
qs.x: She made it a few years before 12 Years a Slave.

qs.q: Chinua Achebe took the title "Things Fall Apart" from a poem by…
qs.x: It's from "The Second Coming". The novel came out in 1958.

qs.q: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o's first novel was…
qs.x: It came out in 1964, and it's often called the first English-language novel by an East African writer.

qs.q: Kenyan-born artist Wangechi Mutu put four bronze sculptures on the front of which New York museum in 2019?
qs.x: The series was called "The NewOnes, will free Us", and they sat in niches that had stood empty for over a century.

qs.q: Why was Genevieve Nnaji's "Lionheart" dropped from the Oscars race in 2019?
a: Too much of it was in English
qs.x: It was Nigeria's first ever entry for the international feature award.

qs.q: "The Woman King" tells the story of the women warriors of which kingdom?
qs.x: Viola Davis plays the general, Nanisca, and Gina Prince-Bythewood directed it.

qs.q: Seydou Keïta's famous studio portraits were shot in which city?
qs.x: He ran his studio from 1948 until the early 1960s, when he became Mali's official government photographer.

qs.q: Denim Tears put the Ghana Must Go check on two classic sneakers this month. Which brand made them?
qs.x: The Stan Smith 80 and Superstar 82 both have a Sankofa heart on the tongue.

qs.q: Mr Eazi's company Choplife Gaming runs which betting brand?
qs.x: He came in as an investor in 2017 and was the face of its ads for years before Choplife took it over.

qs.q: Which payments brand named Joshua Baraka its first Ugandan ambassador in November?
qs.x: It's backing his B'rakaland EA show at Lugogo in Kampala on 28 November.

qs.q: Java House opened its very first coffee shop in 1999 in which Nairobi mall?
qs.x: It was co-founded by Kevin Ashley, an American who'd moved to Kenya.

qs.q: In 2020, Lagos-based Paystack was bought by which US payments company?
qs.x: The deal was worth more than $200 million, the biggest for a Nigerian startup at the time.

qs.q: Stoney Tangawizi, the ginger drink every Kenyan knows, is made by…
qs.x: Tangawizi is just Swahili for ginger.

qs.q: Kenya's Kevian is the company behind which juice?
qs.x: Kimani Rugendo started Kevian in the 1990s with bottled water, before it moved into juice.

qs.q: Mike Adenuga founded which Nigerian network?
qs.x: Glo went live in 2003 and is still Nigerian-owned.

qs.q: In 2017, Kenyan betting firm SportPesa became the shirt sponsor of which Premier League club?
qs.x: The Toffees even played a friendly in Tanzania that summer as part of the deal.

qs.q: Naivas opened its first shop in 1990 at Rongai, just outside which town?
qs.x: It traded as Naivasha Self Service Stores for a while, and that's where the name Naivas comes from.

qs.q: What's the highest peak on Mount Kenya called?
qs.x: Batian stands at 5,199 m. Most trekkers stop at Point Lenana, which is lower.

qs.q: Which country has more pyramids than Egypt?
qs.x: The Nubian pyramids at Meroë are smaller and steeper than the ones at Giza.

qs.q: Next March's FIFA election happens in Morocco's capital. Which city is that?
qs.x: Casablanca is bigger, but Rabat is the capital. The 77th FIFA Congress is there on 18 March 2027.

qs.q: Which of these countries does NOT touch Lake Victoria?
qs.x: Lake Victoria is shared by just three countries. Tanzania holds about half of it.

qs.q: Which country renamed itself Eswatini in 2018?
qs.x: King Mswati III announced it on the 50th anniversary of independence.

qs.q: What's Africa's smallest country by land area?
qs.x: It's only about 455 km², spread across roughly 115 islands in the Indian Ocean.

qs.q: Lake Assal, the lowest point in Africa, is in which country?
qs.x: It sits about 155 m below sea level, and it's one of the saltiest lakes on earth.

qs.q: Which country officially runs on a 13-month calendar?
qs.x: Twelve months of 30 days, then a short one of five or six. New Year falls in September.

qs.q: How many counties does Kenya have?
qs.x: They came with the 2010 constitution and replaced the old provinces.

qs.q: Sossusvlei's big red dunes are in which country?
qs.x: They're in the Namib, which is often called the oldest desert in the world.

qs.q: Joshua Baraka was HiPipo's Artist of the Year in 2026. How many years running is that?
qs.x: He won four awards on the night, including East Africa Best Act/Song for "This Time" with JAE5.

qs.q: Awar Odhiang is the Fashion Awards' Model of the Year 2026. Whose show did she close in October 2025?
qs.x: It was Matthieu Blazy's first show for the house.

qs.q: Messi won the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports this year. Which Kenyan has won it too?
qs.x: Kipchoge won in 2023. Messi is the first footballer to win it alone.

qs.q: Binyavanga Wainaina won the Caine Prize in 2002 with which story?
a: One Day I Will Write About This Place
qs.x: "How to Write About Africa" is his famous satirical essay, and the memoir came later.

qs.q: The first Ibrahim Prize for African leadership went in 2007 to a former president of which country?
qs.x: It went to Joaquim Chissano. In many years since, no one has been judged good enough to win it.

qs.q: Kofi Annan shared the 2001 Nobel Peace Prize with…
qs.x: He was the first UN chief from sub-Saharan Africa.

qs.q: Faith Kipyegon was World Athletics' track athlete of the year for 2023. How many world records did she break that year?
qs.x: The 1500m, the mile and the 5000m, all inside about two months.

qs.q: Which South African-born star won Best Actress at the Oscars for "Monster"?
qs.x: She won in 2004, the first South African to win an acting Oscar.

qs.q: Kenya's Kalasha Awards are for…
qs.x: They're run by the Kenya Film Commission.

qs.q: Who won the first Sócrates Award, for players' work off the pitch, at the 2022 Ballon d'Or?
qs.x: He paid for a hospital and a school in Bambali, the village where he grew up.

qs.q: In 1994 Tegla Loroupe became the first African woman to win a major marathon. Where?
qs.x: She was 21 and it was her first major. She came back and won it again a year later.

qs.q: Romelu Lukaku just retired from Belgium duty. His family's roots run back to which city?
qs.x: His dad, Roger, played for Zaire. Romelu leaves Belgium with 94 goals.

qs.q: The WRC Safari Rally is based around which Kenyan town?
qs.x: It came back to the World Rally Championship in 2021 after 19 years away.

qs.q: In 1988, Ibrahim Hussein became the first African man to win which marathon?
qs.x: The year before, he was the first African man to win New York too.

qs.q: Kip Keino won Olympic 1500m gold in which city?
qs.x: That was 1968. Four years later in Munich he won the steeplechase.

qs.q: Kenya reached the Cricket World Cup semi-finals in which year?
qs.x: They beat Sri Lanka on the way, and India knocked them out in Durban.

qs.q: Which country has won the most men's Rugby World Cups?
Gor Mahia fans call their club…
qs.x: Ingwe is AFC Leopards, the other side of the Mashemeji derby.

qs.q: Tunisia's Ahmed Hafnaoui won Olympic 400m freestyle gold in Tokyo at what age?
qs.x: He went in as the slowest qualifier for the final, swimming from lane eight.

qs.q: Javelin thrower Julius Yego got the nickname "YouTube Man" because…
a: He learned by watching YouTube videos
He went viral for a dance
qs.x: He went on to win the world title in Beijing in 2015.

qs.q: In January 1983, which Nigerian president ordered undocumented migrants out of the country, giving the Ghana Must Go bag its name?
qs.x: About two million people were affected, around half of them Ghanaian, and they had until 31 January to go.

qs.q: The Mau Mau stayed officially banned in Kenya until which year?
qs.x: Independence came in 1963, but the ban stayed on the books for another 40 years.

qs.q: The 1884–85 conference where European powers carved up Africa was held in which city?
qs.x: Fourteen countries sent delegates. Not a single African was invited.

qs.q: Before Nairobi, which town was the capital of what became Kenya?
qs.x: Nairobi started life in 1899 as a depot on the railway.

qs.q: Which Asante queen mother led the War of the Golden Stool against the British in 1900?
qs.x: She was queen mother of Ejisu, and a well-known girls' school in Kumasi is named after her.

qs.q: Which woman ruled ancient Egypt as pharaoh and built the temple at Deir el-Bahari?
qs.x: She's often shown in statues wearing the pharaoh's false beard.

qs.q: Who was Kenya's first woman elected to parliament?
qs.x: She won the Kisumu seat in 1969, after being the city's first woman mayor.

qs.q: South Africa held its first election open to all races in which year?
qs.x: It was 27 April, which is now Freedom Day.

qs.q: The Suez Canal opened in which year?
qs.x: 1956 is the year Egypt nationalised it, which set off the Suez Crisis.

qs.q: Who built Fort Jesus in Mombasa?
qs.x: They built it in the 1590s to guard the harbour. The Omanis took it in 1698 after a siege of nearly three years.

qs.q: Tems is the executive music producer on the soundtrack for which film?
qs.x: She also wrote and sings the lead single, "African Love Story". The film reaches cinemas in January.

qs.q: Youssou N'Dour's biggest international hit, "7 Seconds", was a duet with…
qs.x: It came out in 1994, and it's sung in Wolof, French and English.

qs.q: Which drummer did Fela Kuti say Afrobeat couldn't exist without?
qs.x: Tony Allen drummed in Fela's band Africa 70 through the 1970s, and Fela credited him as a co-creator of the sound.

qs.q: Hugh Masekela was best known for playing which instrument?
qs.x: His 1968 instrumental "Grazing in the Grass" went all the way to number one in the US.

qs.q: Burna Boy's "Last Last" is built on a sample of which singer's song?
qs.x: It flips Toni Braxton's "He Wasn't Man Enough" from 2000.

qs.q: Ethic Entertainment's "Lamba Lolo" helped put which Kenyan sound on the map?
qs.x: It went viral in 2018, and the matatus played it on repeat.

qs.q: In 2021, UNESCO added which music to its intangible cultural heritage list?
qs.x: DR Congo and the Republic of Congo put in the bid together, and it was approved in December 2021.

qs.q: Zuchu's mother is which famous taarab singer?
qs.x: Zuchu grew up around taarab in Zanzibar before Diamond Platnumz signed her to WCB Wasafi.

qs.q: Kabza De Small and DJ Maphorisa team up under which name?
qs.x: Their joint albums helped take amapiano from South Africa's townships to the rest of the world.

qs.q: Ayra Starr is signed to which Nigerian label?
qs.x: Mavin is Don Jazzy's label, the same home that gave us Rema.

qs.q: In the 1987 TV version of "Things Fall Apart", Pete Edochie played…
qs.x: The role gave him the name Ebubedike, which stayed with him until he died last week at 79.

qs.q: Which South African actor plays Zélie in "Children of Blood and Bone"?
qs.x: The film is set in Orïsha, a world built on the Yoruba Orisha tradition, and it opens in January.

qs.q: What was Netflix's first Kenyan original series?
qs.x: The drama came out in 2022 and follows a woman who goes home to her village to fight a mining company.

qs.q: Which 1992 film is usually credited with starting Nollywood's home video boom?
qs.x: It was made in Igbo and sold on VHS tapes straight to people's homes.

qs.q: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's "Half of a Yellow Sun" is set during which war?
qs.x: The film version starred Chiwetel Ejiofor and Thandiwe Newton.

qs.q: The painter Chéri Samba, famous for his bright paintings with speech bubbles, is from which country?
qs.x: He started out painting signs and comic strips in Kinshasa in the 1970s.

qs.q: Zeitz MOCAA, Africa's big contemporary art museum, was built inside an old…
qs.x: It opened in Cape Town's V&A Waterfront in 2017.

qs.q: Mati Diop's "Atlantics" won which prize at Cannes in 2019?
qs.x: She was the first Black woman director to have a film in the main competition.

qs.q: "Vioja Mahakamani", the KBC comedy, is set mostly in a…
qs.x: Mahakamani means in court, and the show ran on Kenyan TV for decades.

qs.q: "Sarafina!" (1992) starred Leleti Khumalo alongside which Hollywood star?
qs.x: It's set around the 1976 Soweto uprising, and it started life as a stage musical.

qs.q: Youssou N'Dour's media group owns RFM radio, TFM television and which daily paper?
qs.x: He built Groupe Futurs Médias in the early 2000s. TFM only got on air in 2010 after a long standoff with the government.

qs.q: Adelle Onyango's Legally Clueless became the first East African podcast to air on radio. Which station picked it up?
qs.x: Kiss FM was where she used to host breakfast. Forbes wrote about the business behind the show in November.

qs.q: Strive Masiyiwa founded which telecoms group?
qs.x: He fought Zimbabwe's government for years for a mobile licence before Econet finally launched in 1998.

qs.q: Who co-founded Flutterwave and is still its CEO?
qs.x: Everyone calls him GB. Aboyeji was a co-founder too but left in 2018.

qs.q: Safaricom listed on the Nairobi bourse in which year?
qs.x: When trading started that June, it was the biggest share sale East Africa had ever seen.

qs.q: Andela, the company that trains and places software developers, was started in which city?
qs.x: It launched in 2014, and Mark Zuckerberg's foundation later backed it.

qs.q: Brookside, Kenya's biggest dairy, is linked to which family?
qs.x: France's Danone bought a stake in it in 2014.

qs.q: The Dangote oil refinery is in which city?
qs.x: It sits in the Lekki Free Trade Zone and is built to handle 650,000 barrels a day.

qs.q: M-KOPA started out in 2011 selling what, paid off bit by bit through M-Pesa?
qs.x: Phones came later. Now it's mostly smartphones on the same pay-as-you-go plan.

qs.q: Bidco, the company behind Elianto oil, is based in which Kenyan town?
qs.x: Vimal Shah chairs it. His father started the business.

qs.q: How many official languages does South Africa have?
qs.x: Sign language became number twelve in 2023.

qs.q: Which is the only African country with Spanish as an official language?
qs.x: It was a Spanish colony until 1968.

qs.q: What sits in the middle of Kenya's flag?
a: A Maasai shield and two spears
qs.x: The shield and spears stand for defending the country's freedom.

qs.q: Which is Africa's deepest lake?
qs.x: It goes down to about 1,470 m, second only to Lake Baikal in the whole world.

qs.q: Which country produces the most coffee in Africa?
qs.x: It's also where coffee comes from in the first place.

qs.q: Liberia's capital, Monrovia, is named after…
qs.x: James Monroe was the US president when the settlement was founded in the 1820s.

qs.q: Victoria Falls sits on the border between which two countries?
qs.x: Locally it's called Mosi-oa-Tunya, the smoke that thunders.

qs.q: What's the capital of Madagascar?
qs.x: People just call it Tana.

qs.q: Ouarzazate, where films like "Gladiator" were shot, is in which country?
qs.x: It's called the door of the desert, and it has some of the biggest film studios in Africa.

qs.q: Timbuktu, the old city of scholars and manuscripts, is in which country?
qs.x: It sits near the Niger River, at the edge of the Sahara.

qs.q: Beyoncé just became the first artist to reach how many Grammy nominations?
qs.x: Number 100 was for "Morning Dew (Donk)". The winners are named on 7 February.

qs.q: Before this week's CAF Awards, Sadio Mané had won African Player of the Year in which two years?
qs.x: The 2026 ceremony was in Lagos on Wednesday, at the National Theatre.

qs.q: Tems won the Grammy for Best African Music Performance in 2025 with which song?
qs.x: She's up for four more in February.

qs.q: Ben Okri won the Booker Prize in 1991 with which novel?
a: Season of Migration to the North
qs.x: He was 32, one of the youngest winners the prize has had.

qs.q: Which South African writer won the Booker twice?
qs.x: First for "Life & Times of Michael K" in 1983, then "Disgrace" in 1999. He got the Nobel in 2003.

qs.q: Nelson Mandela and F.W. de Klerk shared the Nobel Peace Prize in which year?
qs.x: That was the year before the first all-race election.

qs.q: Which Ethiopian leader won the 2019 Nobel Peace Prize?
qs.x: It was mainly for ending the long standoff with Eritrea.

qs.q: "My Octopus Teacher", which won the Oscar for best documentary in 2021, was filmed off the coast of which country?
qs.x: Craig Foster filmed it in a kelp forest near Cape Town.

qs.q: Peter Tabichi, the Kenyan science teacher who won the 2019 Global Teacher Prize, took home how much?
qs.x: He's a Franciscan brother who taught at a village school in Nakuru County and gave most of his pay away.

qs.q: Who has won CAF Women's Player of the Year a record six times?
qs.x: Perpetua Nkwocha is next on the list, with four.

qs.q: Who finished as top scorer at AFCON 2025 in Morocco?
qs.x: The Real Madrid forward made the CAF Player of the Year final five too.

qs.q: Bayern Munich signed Morocco's Ismael Saibari in July from which club?
qs.x: He'd just scored in all three of Morocco's World Cup group games.

qs.q: Which club has won the CAF Champions League the most times?
qs.x: Zamalek and TP Mazembe are next, with five each.

qs.q: Ferdinand Omanyala set his African 100m record of 9.77 in which city?
qs.x: It was at the Kip Keino Classic at Kasarani in September 2021.

qs.q: Who won Kenya's first ever Olympic gold?
qs.x: He won the 10,000m at Mexico City in 1968, a few days before Keino's 1500m.

qs.q: Which city hosted the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympic event ever held in Africa?
qs.x: The Games ran in Senegal from 31 October to 13 November.

qs.q: In 2018, Siya Kolisi became the Springboks' first Black…
qs.x: He then lifted the World Cup twice, in 2019 and 2023.

qs.q: Kyalami, the last track to host a Formula 1 race in Africa, is in which country?
qs.x: The last South African Grand Prix there was in 1993.

qs.q: Hakeem Olajuwon, the No. 1 pick in the 1984 NBA draft, was born in which city?
qs.x: He took the Houston Rockets to two NBA titles, in 1994 and 1995.

qs.q: In 2024, Biniam Girmay became the first Black African to win a stage of the Tour de France. Where is he from?
qs.x: He won three stages that year and took the green jersey home to Asmara.

qs.q: Who was Kenya's first vice-president?
qs.x: He served from 1964 until he resigned in 1966 and started his own party, the KPU.

qs.q: The rock-cut churches of Lalibela are in which country?
qs.x: Tradition credits King Lalibela, who ruled around 1200. They were carved straight down into the rock.

qs.q: Patrice Lumumba was the first prime minister of which country?
qs.x: He took office at independence in June 1960 and was killed in January 1961.

qs.q: Kenya's Saba Saba rally of 7 July 1990 pushed for…
qs.x: A year and a half later, in December 1991, the one-party law was scrapped.

qs.q: South Africa marks the Sharpeville massacre of 21 March 1960 with which public holiday?
qs.x: Police opened fire on people protesting the pass laws, and 69 were killed.

qs.q: What does "Burkina Faso" mean?
qs.x: Thomas Sankara picked the name in 1984 to replace Upper Volta.

qs.q: Which Kenyan city was first called Port Florence?
qs.x: The Uganda Railway reached the lake there in December 1901.

qs.q: Which king built the Zulu nation into a big power in the early 1800s?
qs.x: Dingane was his half-brother, and he killed Shaka in 1828 and took over.

qs.q: Steve Biko led which movement in South Africa?
qs.x: He died in police custody in 1977, aged 30.

qs.q: Before he was crowned, Emperor Haile Selassie was known as…
qs.x: That's where the Rastafari movement in Jamaica got its name.
